permutationLabel: Iron-deficiency anaemia, post-menopausal, no GI symptoms
summary: 64-year-old post-menopausal woman with fatigue, Hb 9.4, MCV 71, ferritin 5 and no GI symptoms. BSG 2021: bidirectional endoscopy (OGD + colonoscopy) and coeliac serology, regardless of FIT.

inputs.hpi: Four months of tiredness and breathlessness climbing hills. Blood test showed anaemia with low iron. No abdominal pain, bowels regular, no blood seen, no black stools, no weight loss. Post-menopausal for 12 years, no vaginal bleeding. Eats meat. No NSAIDs. FIT 8 µg Hb/g.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Iron-deficiency anaemia, cause unknown
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Iron-deficiency anaemia (Hb 9.4, ferritin 5) in a post-menopausal woman without GI symptoms. Needs bidirectional endoscopy and coeliac serology.

mustInclude.note: BSG 2021: bidirectional endoscopy in post-menopausal women with IDA (gastric cancer is the other must-not-miss).

guideline.name: BSG guideline — management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults
guideline.section: IDA in men and post-menopausal women: bidirectional endoscopy; coeliac serology; iron replacement
guideline.citation: Snook J, Bhala N, Beales ILP, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for the management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults. Gut. 2021;70:2030–2051.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: age ≥ 60 with iron-deficiency anaemia
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

guideline.name: ACPGBI/BSG joint guideline — FIT in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer
guideline.section: IDA is referred irrespective of the FIT result
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Davies MM, Abulafi M, et al. Faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer (CRC): a joint guideline from the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI) and the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG). Gut. 2022;71:1939–1962.

rationale: Permutation: laboratory-only presentation (Hb, MCV, ferritin) with a sub-threshold FIT. The only chips are fatigue and breathlessness; the engines must read the labs to reach the colorectal pathway.

authoring.author: Claude (colorectal/anorectal cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations verified: false until checked against the source.
